notes: Four parallel lane sweeps (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security), each pre-checked against data/manifest.json, the three most recent run logs, and the full text of data/events/2026-09.json through 2026-11.json (security and devtools/cloud lanes also checked 2026-12 through 2027-03 given the deadlines they were chasing). All direct WebFetch attempts hit the expected EGRESS_BLOCKED except a couple of resolvable developer/help pages; every entry below rests on a search result that quoted or cited a primary source, or reputable secondary reporting when the primary wasn't reachable. Sept 4-5 was quiet for genuinely new AI/bigtech announcements beyond what prior runs already filed, so this run leans toward forward-dated corrections and previously-unfiled retirement/deadline dates rather than fresh announcement-kind entries. Caught one cross-lane duplicate before filing: both the ai and devtools/cloud lanes independently found Google Cloud's Vertex AI Extensions shutdown (2026-11-26) -- filed once. Also caught that the ai lane's NVIDIA GTC 2027 candidate is already on the calendar (2027-03.json) at confidence 'expected' from the same nvidia.com/gtc/faq source the lane found again this run -- since that page states the dates directly rather than merely signalling them, filed a correction upgrading it to 'confirmed' rather than a duplicate. Reframed the bigtech/hardware/mobile lane's HTC Vive Eagle finding: the lane surfaced a Sept 3 US on-sale date, which is outside the yesterday/today window for an announcement-kind entry, but the same reporting gives a genuinely future UK/Europe/Australia ship date (Sept 21) -- filed that as an event instead of dropping the finding entirely. Dropped the ai lane's GitHub Copilot 'October 2 retirement wave' candidate (Gemini 3.5/3.6 Flash, Kimi K2.7 Code, Claude Opus 4.7): its only source was a single aggregator site with no github.blog post or other corroboration, and the specific model-name claims are exactly the kind of detail that's risky to file on secondary sourcing alone -- below the bar even at 'rumored'. Corrected two mobile-topic mistags from lane agents per routine/sources.md's own table (a phone/glasses launch is hardware, not mobile) before filing: Xiaomi 18 Fold and HTC Vive Eagle are filed as hardware-only.
concerns: The devtools/cloud lane filed three Azure Maps retirement entries dated within two weeks of each other (Render V1 API on 09-17, Web SDK Map Control v1.x on 09-19, Map Control 2.0.x + Service Module on 09-30), all sharing the tokens 'Azure Maps'/'Map Control'. Titled them with maximally distinct wording to dodge src/lib/id.ts's sameTitle() near-duplicate weighting bug (flagged in the 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-04 run logs for SKU-name collisions), but this is a workaround, not a fix -- the same three real, distinct retirements would be at real risk of merging into one row if titled more naturally. Worth the maintainer fix already flagged twice: weight tokens with version numbers/model suffixes more heavily in the similarity score.

Confirmed this run that the same sameTitle() weighting bug hits model-name variants, not just SKU/version variants: a straightforward 'Claude Haiku 4.5 reaches minimum support floor' and 'Claude Opus 4.5 reaches minimum support floor' both dry-ran as updates to the already-filed 'Claude Sonnet 4.5 reaches minimum support floor' (2026-09-29) -- same org, same generic phrase, differing only on the model name (haiku/opus/sonnet), which is exactly the pattern already flagged for SKUs. Retitled both to 'Claude Haiku 4.5 hits end of guaranteed API support' and 'Claude Opus 4.5 exits minimum guaranteed support window' to clear the 0.6 threshold and filed them as new entries instead of corrupting Sonnet 4.5's row. This will keep recurring for every future Anthropic/OpenAI/Google model-family deprecation wave (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus, mini/nano/pro, etc.) until model-name tokens are weighted like the SKU/version tokens already flagged.
